# 0091 — The `.msh` recipe block: logo, generated by, the assembly description

- **Status:** done
- **Decision:** [0038 — Mesh files carry their recipe](../decisions/0038-mesh-files-carry-their-recipe.md); decision 0001 (the intent layer, `to_dict`)
- **Depends on:** —

Ground rules for all tasks: [README](README.md#ground-rules).  This task
works in `hexmesh/io/writers/`, `hexmesh/assembly/assembler.py`,
`hexmesh/assembly/intent.py`, `tests/`, `API.md`.

**Why.**  A `.msh` written by hexmesh says nothing about where it came
from.  Decision 0038 puts the logo, a "generated by" line and the
recipe (`Assembly.to_dict()`) into a `$Comments` block, so the mesh
rebuilds itself.  The design session checked the readers
(`docs/integrations/gmsh.md` and `openfoam.md`, 2026-11-02): gmsh and
`gmshToFoam` (v1912, v2406) skip the block.  gmsh keeps it on re-save
but re-wraps lines longer than 255 characters.

**Where.**
- New `hexmesh/io/writers/msh_comments.py` (or similar): writes and
  reads the block.  It takes a dict and strings and knows nothing about
  assemblies (DESIGN §3.1: `io.writers` is a leaf).
- `Assembly.write` and `write_openfoam` (`assembly/assembler.py`) call
  it after `gmsh.write`.
- `read_recipe(path)` and `Assembly.from_msh(path)`.

**Do.**
1. **The block**, inserted right after `$EndMeshFormat`:
   ```text
   $Comments
   <docs/ascii-logo.txt, byte for byte>
   generated by hexmesh <__version__> (gmsh <gmsh.__version__>, MSH <2.2|4.1> <ASCII|binary>)
   write: <write|write_openfoam> dim=… interfaces=… walls_by_fitting=…
   hexmesh-recipe-begin
   <compact JSON, separators=(",", ":"), wrapped at 200 characters>
   hexmesh-recipe-end
   $EndComments
   ```
   - The logo ships with the package, not read from `docs/` at run
     time.  Add a test that the shipped copy equals
     `docs/ascii-logo.txt`.
   - No content line starts with `$`; assert it before writing.
   - No timestamp, host, user or path.
   - In a binary file, insert the block after the text
     `$EndMeshFormat\n` and its binary marker line.  Check how gmsh
     writes that header, and record it in `docs/integrations/gmsh.md`.
2. **Unserialisable assemblies:** if `to_dict` raises (`TypeError`), write
   `recipe: not serialisable (<message>)` in place of the recipe
   lines.  The write still succeeds, with no warning.
3. **`provenance=True`** keyword on `write` and `write_openfoam`;
   `False` writes the file exactly as today.
4. **Read-back:** `read_recipe(path) -> dict | None` joins the lines
   between the markers, removing all newlines, and parses JSON.  It
   returns `None` when there is no block or no recipe.
   `Assembly.from_msh(path)` = `from_dict(read_recipe(path))`, with a
   clear error when there is no recipe.
   - It must work on a file gmsh has re-saved: the block moved and
     re-wrapped at 255 characters.
   - Never `eval`.  Read in text mode for ASCII and in binary mode for
     binary files; read only up to `$EndComments`.
5. **API.md** documents the block, `provenance=`, `read_recipe` and
   `from_msh`.

**Accept.**
- Round-trip: for every `hexmesh/examples` script that writes a mesh
  (or builds one), write → `from_msh` → write gives a **byte-identical**
  `.msh`.  Do this for both `write` and `write_openfoam`.
- The same after a gmsh re-save in 2.2 ASCII, 4.1 ASCII and 4.1 binary:
  `read_recipe` returns the same dict.
- `provenance=False` gives the same bytes as today's writer.
- A block with an extra, unknown line (outside the recipe markers)
  gives the same `read_recipe` result.  Decision 0038's deferred points
  will arrive as extra lines.
- `gmshToFoam` gives the same `polyMesh` with and without the block
  (`-m openfoam`, v2406; v1912 if installed).
- An unserialisable assembly writes, with the "not serialisable" line.
- `tests/test_architecture.py` passes: the helper imports nothing from
  `assembly`.
- Full suite: no new failures.  If any test compares `.msh` bytes or
  checksums against stored files, list them in *Outcome* with what you
  regenerated.

**Out of scope.**  OpenFOAM writers' banner, and the source of
network-built assemblies (decision 0038, deferred).

## Agent notes

- **Line endings (decision 0039, from the design session 2026-11-02).**
  The `.msh` post-processing keeps the file's own line endings: the
  helper reads and writes the file in binary only (`read_bytes` /
  `write_bytes`, `open(..., "rb")`), and writes `\n` itself.  No text-mode
  I/O is added; any text read or write this task adds passes
  `encoding="utf-8"`.  So the byte-identical round-trip holds on Windows
  too, not only by accident on Linux.
- **The version moved to a leaf**, `hexmesh/version.py`, re-exported as
  `hexmesh.__version__`.  `assembly` stamps it without importing the root
  package.  `tests/test_architecture.py`: `hexmesh.version` added to the
  shared leaves, and the private-name rule now treats dunders
  (`__version__`) as public, with a planted case.

- **`$` in the recipe is escaped** as `\u0024`.  Wrapping at 200
  characters could otherwise put a `$` from a string value (a name) at
  the start of a line and end the block early.  JSON reads the escape
  back as `$`; outside strings, JSON never contains `$`.  The "no line
  starts with `$`" assertion therefore guards only the fixed lines.
- **The round-trip's second write** takes `walls_by_fitting` from the
  block's `write:` line; `from_msh` returns only the assembly.

## Questions for design

## Outcome

Done 2026-11-02.  Every Accept item holds.

**Files.**
- New:
  - `hexmesh/io/writers/msh_comments.py`: `block`, `insert`,
    `msh_format`, `read_recipe`, and the shipped logo `LOGO_LINES`.
    Binary I/O only (decision 0039).
  - `hexmesh/version.py`: `__version__`, moved out of
    `hexmesh/__init__.py`, which re-exports it.
  - `tests/test_msh_recipe.py`: 46 tests (2 of them `-m openfoam`).
- Changed:
  - `hexmesh/assembly/assembler.py`: `provenance=True` on `write` and
    `write_openfoam`, `_stamp`, `Assembly.from_msh`;
  - `hexmesh/io/__init__.py`, `hexmesh/io/writers/__init__.py`: export
    `read_recipe`;
  - `tests/test_architecture.py`: `hexmesh.version` is a shared leaf, and
    dunders are public under the private-name rule;
  - `API.md`;
  - `docs/integrations/gmsh.md`: the binary header;
  - `docs/integrations/openfoam.md`: `gmshToFoam` crashes on a missing
    file.
- `assembly/intent.py` needed no change.

**Acceptance.**
- **Round trip:** for all 28 examples, write → `from_msh` → write is
  byte-identical, for `write` and for `write_openfoam`.  Covered by
  `test_example_round_trip_is_byte_identical`, 28 cases, about 3 min.
- **gmsh re-save** in 2.2 ASCII, 4.1 ASCII and 4.1 binary: `read_recipe`
  returns the same dict.
- **`provenance=False`** equals a plain `gmsh.write` of the same mesh.
  The provenance file minus the block equals it too, for ASCII, binary
  and `write_openfoam`.
- **Unknown lines** before and after the markers, and another tool's
  `$Comments` block before ours, give the same `read_recipe` result.
- **`gmshToFoam`:** the same `polyMesh` (every file, byte for byte) with
  and without the block, on v1912 (native) and v2406 (Docker).
- **An unserialisable assembly** (an unregistered `Straight` subclass)
  writes `recipe: not serialisable (cannot serialise fitting type
  _Unregistered)`, with no warning.  `read_recipe` returns None, and
  `from_msh` raises a `ValueError` saying why.
- **gmsh reads** a file with the block (ASCII and binary) with the same
  nodes, hexes and groups as one without it.
- **Binary header:** gmsh writes the endianness marker (`01 00 00 00`)
  and `\n` before `$EndMeshFormat\n`, and the block goes after that.
  Recorded in `docs/integrations/gmsh.md`.
- **Architecture:** `test_architecture.py` passes (24); the helper imports
  nothing from `assembly`.
- **Byte comparisons:** no test compares `.msh` bytes or checksums
  against stored files.  `test_study`'s hashes are of variant
  parameters.  Nothing was regenerated.
- **Full suite:** 2245 passed, 15 skipped (+44), no failures.  The 4 extra
  warnings are the examples' own narrow-wye warnings, raised again by
  the round trip.

**Disk space.**
- The example round-trip trial wrote about 180 MB of meshes to my
  scratchpad.  Those, the header probes and the `gmshToFoam` probe case
  are deleted, along with task 0081's leftover recorder meshes
  (129 MB).  12 KB of scripts remain.
- The test runs write under pytest's `tmp_path`, which pytest prunes to
  its last three runs.  The latest run's directory is about 240 MB.
- Free space after cleanup: 42 GB.

**Surprises.**
- `gmshToFoam` crashes on a missing file instead of reporting it: v1912
  segfaults, v2406 says "Cannot dereference nullptr".  My first v2406
  test hit this because the `.msh` directory wasn't mounted.
- Meshing the same assembly twice in one gmsh session fails ("Surface 1
  is transfinite but has 8 corners").  The tests write each file in its
  own session.  Existing behaviour, not changed here.

**Proposed follow-ups.**
- A `write:` reader (`read_write_options`), so `from_msh` users can
  repeat the write without parsing the line themselves.
- 0092's encoding rule will also cover `foam_case`-style test helpers
  that write text without `encoding=`.  This task's new test writes
  bytes.
